lessons.title: Tool descriptions that get picked
lessons.eli5: Claude chooses tools by reading their descriptions, like picking a drawer by its label. Clear labels mean the right drawer gets opened.
lessons.body:
## The description is the interface

Claude never sees your implementation. It sees a **name**, a **description** and an **input schema**. Good descriptions say:

- what the tool does and does *not* do;
- when to use it instead of a similar tool;
- what each parameter means, with formats and examples.

## Overlapping tools

Two tools with vague, similar descriptions cause misrouting. Either merge them or sharpen the boundary in both descriptions.
keyTakeaways: Tool selection accuracy depends mostly on description quality.
examTips: If the model keeps picking the wrong tool, the first fix is the description, not the model.
commonTraps: Adding few-shot examples to the system prompt before fixing the tool descriptions.

lessons.title: MCP hosts, clients and servers
lessons.eli5: MCP is a universal plug. The app you use is the host, it opens a client connection, and each server is a tool box you plug in.
lessons.body:
## Three roles

- **Host**: the application the user interacts with (for example an IDE or chat app).
- **Client**: lives inside the host and holds one connection to one server.
- **Server**: exposes tools, resources and prompts.

## Transports

| Transport | Use when |
| --- | --- |
| stdio | The server runs locally as a subprocess |
| Streamable HTTP | The server is remote or shared by many users |
keyTakeaways: stdio for local, HTTP for remote.
examTips: Questions about sharing a server across a team usually point to HTTP transport.
commonTraps: Confusing the host with the server.
